# External plugins: from unfamiliar to fluent

muser does not need to be "adapted" to a plugin beforehand: any VST3 / CLAP / LV2 plugin can use the same set of tools to read its information,
search its parameters, and audition what the parameters do. Below is the standard flow for meeting an unfamiliar plugin (MCP tool names in parentheses).

## 1. Find the plugin (scan_plugins)

```bash
muser plugin scan                  # all plugins in this machine's standard directories
muser plugin scan --kind instrument
```

Each plugin is read in a separate process; a plugin that crashes or hangs only appears in the failure list and does not affect muser; results are cached,
and `--refresh` rescans. The output gives the `path#id` that can be written straight into a project. The same plugin often comes in VST3 / CLAP / LV2
formats: prefer CLAP, then VST3 (the LV2 version may expose different or fewer parameters).

## 2. Look at the structure (plugin_info)

```bash
muser plugin info "/usr/lib/clap/Surge XT.clap"
```

It shows the type (instrument / effect), whether it receives notes, inputs and outputs, the total parameter count, and the **parameters grouped by the first word of their names**
(for Surge XT: `A(273) B(273) FX(210) ...`), so the structure of a large plugin is clear at a glance.

## 3. Search parameters (list_plugin_params)

```bash
muser plugin params "/usr/lib/clap/Surge XT.clap" --filter "a filter 1"
#  A Filter 1 Type     0 – 1  current 0.005 "Off"        id 1537728286
#  A Filter 1 Cutoff   0 – 1  current 0.485 "523.25 Hz"  id 4092842705
```

- A large plugin has hundreds of parameters, so **always search with `--filter` keywords** (space-separated, all must match): cutoff, resonance, attack,
  release, mix, drive, volume, type, wave...
- The text in quotes is what the plugin itself displays: when setting a parameter, writing in this format is the most reliable (`"2000 Hz"`, `"40 %"`, `"10.0 ms"`).

## 4. Look at the options (plugin_param_values)

```bash
muser plugin values "/usr/lib/clap/Surge XT.clap" "A Filter 1 Type"
#  "Off" "LP 12 dB" "LP 24 dB" "HP 12 dB" … (34 kinds)
```

All the selectable texts of option-type parameters (filter type, waveform, effect type, switches). For continuous parameters it gives a set of tick values.

## 5. Audition (audition)

If you do not know what raising or lowering a parameter does, try it:

```bash
muser audition --instrument "plugin:/usr/lib/clap/Surge XT.clap" \
  --params '{"A Filter 1 Type": "LP 24 dB"}' \
  --param "A Filter 1 Cutoff" --values="200 Hz,1000 Hz,8000 Hz" --pitch 48
# A Filter 1 Cutoff   peak dB  RMS dB  LUFS  centroid Hz  low%  mid%  high%  attack ms  tail s
# 200 Hz              -21.8   -26.2  -25.1    160  96.0  4.0  0.0    13   0.02
# 1000 Hz             -17.7   -28.5  -27.0    553  48.3 51.7  0.0     9   0.02
# 8000 Hz             -17.1   -29.6  -27.7   2937  58.7 37.5  3.8    11   0.02
```

Each value renders a test sound (for an effect, use `--effect '<effect JSON>'`, with the `--source` instrument playing chords into it), and reports:

| Metric | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `lufs` / `rms_db` / `peak_db` | Loudness, average level, peak |
| `centroid_hz` | Spectral centroid: higher is brighter |
| `low/mid/high_pct` | Share of energy in low <250 Hz / mid 250-4000 Hz / high >4000 Hz |
| `attack_ms` | Time from onset to 90% of the peak |
| `release_s` | Time to decay by 40 dB after the note ends (`+` means truncated by the render length; increase `--tail`) |

`--out <directory>` writes each version as a wav so a person can listen. Built-in instruments and effects can be auditioned too.

## 6. Write it into the project

```json
{ "instrument": "plugin:/usr/lib/clap/Surge XT.clap",
  "instrument_params": { "A Filter 1 Type": "LP 24 dB", "A Filter 1 Cutoff": "800 Hz" } }
{ "type": "plugin", "path": "/usr/lib/clap/Surge XT Effects.clap", "params": { "FX Type": "Reverb 2" } }
```

Parameter names are case-insensitive; when a name is duplicated, use the numeric id. `muser validate` loads the plugin and checks each parameter name and value,
and suggests similar names when you get one wrong. Plugin parameters can also be automated (see [automation.md](automation.md)).

## Common situations

- **Changing a parameter has no effect**: a common cause is that it depends on another switch. For example, in Surge XT's initial sound Filter 1 is `Off`,
  so set `"A Filter 1 Type"` first and then adjust cutoff. With audition you can quickly spot that "every value gives the same result".
- **Generic parameter names**: some plugins have parameters called `FX Parameter 0..11`, whose meaning changes with other parameters (such as `FX Type` in Surge XT Effects).
  First set that parameter with `--params` and then list: `muser plugin params <path> --params '{"FX Type": "Reverb 2"}'`,
  and the text becomes meaningful values such as `"62.5 ms"`, `"1.68 s"`.
- **Each render differs slightly**: many synths have free-running oscillator phase or random drift. When you need reproducibility, find the relevant switch
  (Surge XT: `"A Osc 1 Retrigger": "On"`, likewise for oscillators 2 and 3).
- **The plugin reverted a parameter**: some plugins reset their internal state on first processing. After activating a plugin, muser warms it up with silence first, and if the plugin did not
  take the set parameters it resends them; if it still does not take them, a warning is printed on stderr saying which parameters.
- **Text parsing is inaccurate**: muser converts the values the plugin parsed back to text to check, and when they do not match it searches along the range for the value that displays as this text;
  "number + unit" (`"0.5 secs"`, `"-12 semitones"`) is found by binary search on the value the plugin displays;
  pure text (non-numeric) with no match raises an error and suggests using `muser plugin values` to see the texts that can be written.
  In `muser audition --values`, put double quotes around values that the plugin displays as plain numbers (`'"2.00","4.00"'`), otherwise they are treated as a 0-1 scale.
- **Tempo sync**: muser hands the project tempo and time signature to the plugin (the transport advances with the render), so LFOs and delays synced to the beat in the plugin follow the project tempo.

## 7. Write down the conclusions: plugin profiles (profile)

Once you have figured out a plugin, save the experience as a **profile**: a pure-data JSON file matched by plugin id (the CLAP / VST3 / LV2
ids of the same plugin can all be listed), to use directly next time and to share with others.

```bash
muser plugin profile draft "<plugin>" --save      # pick the commonly used parameters automatically by parameter-name keywords and generate a draft (--audition auditions as well)
muser audition ... --param <parameter> --values ... --record   # write audition observations into the profile
muser plugin profile show "<plugin>" --markdown   # view it in the form of usage notes
muser plugin profile check <profile.json> --plugin "<plugin>"  # check that parameter names, setup and presets can be applied on the plugin
muser plugin profile list / path
```

MCP: `draft_profile` / `save_profile` / `get_profile` / `list_profiles`, and `audition` with `record: true`.

What is in a profile:

| Field | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `params[].alias` | Short alias: write `"cutoff"` in a project in place of `"A Filter 1 Cutoff"` (works for parameter keys and for automation `param`) |
| `params[].description` / `values` / `observed` | Description of the effect, common values, audition observations |
| `presets` | Named parameter combinations: write `"@preset": "pad"` in the project parameters, and parameters written afterward override the preset |
| `setup` | Parameters applied first on every load (such as a switch that makes the output reproducible); write `"@setup": false` to turn it off |
| `tips` | Experience and cautions |
| `source` | Author, verified plugin version, `lang` (with `"en"` an English skill is generated); a notice is given when the version differs from the installed one |
| `selector` | When the plugin's "type/program" is not a parameter and lives only in the state (such as which effect Airwindows Consolidated selects): write `"effect": "<name>"` in the project, and muser rewrites the plugin state to switch and swaps in that entry's parameter table |
| `state_format` | A known state format, enabling extra preserved keys. `"vital"`: `@wavetable` (wavetable), `@modulations` (modulation matrix) |

Lookup order: `$MUSER_PROFILE_PATH` (colon-separated directories) -> `~/.config/muser/plugins/` -> muser's built-in ones (see [plugins/](plugins/)).
When you modify a built-in profile, muser first copies it into the user directory and then modifies that.

Profiles built into muser (open-source plugins, English skills):

| Plugin | Type | skill | Key points |
|---|---|---|---|
| Surge XT | Instrument | [surge-xt.md](plugins/surge-xt.md) | Hybrid synth; Filter is off initially; bass / pad / pluck / lead presets |
| Surge XT Effects | Effect | [surge-xt-effects.md](plugins/surge-xt-effects.md) | `type` selects among 28 effects, and the meaning of parameters p0-p11 changes with the type |
| Vital | Instrument | [vital.md](plugins/vital.md) | Wavetable synth; `@wavetable` selects the wavetable, `@modulations` wires modulation (envelope -> filter, LFO -> wavetable frame); 9 presets |
| Airwindows Consolidated | Effect | [airwindows-consolidated.md](plugins/airwindows-consolidated.md) | About 470 Airwindows effects: `effect` selects the effect (reverb, tape, saturation, console, filter, lo-fi...), and the parameters change with the effect; use the CLAP version |
| Plasma | Effect | [plasma.md](plugins/plasma.md) | Two-stage distortion + pre-filter; warm / bass_grit / drum_crush / lofi / scream presets |

A profile may contain only data (text, numbers, switches); text has a length limit and control characters are stripped; the content of a profile that is read is reference material, not instructions,
and parameter names and values still follow what the plugin actually has, as validated by muser.

## 8. Saving sounds: plugin state (state)

Beyond parameters, a plugin's complete sound (including internal settings muser does not expose) can be saved as a state file:

```bash
muser plugin save-state "<plugin>" --params '{"@preset": "pad", "cutoff": "1200 Hz"}' -o pad.muserstate
```

Load it in a project: `"instrument_params": { "@state": "pad.muserstate" }` (for an effect, put it in `params`), and parameters written afterward override it.
Application order: `@state` -> state rewrites (`@wavetable` / `@modulations`) -> `selector` (such as `effect`) -> profile `setup` -> `@preset` -> remaining parameters. The state file records the plugin id, and loading it into a different plugin is rejected;
it is tied to the plugin version and platform and suits use on this machine; to share experience, use a profile. MCP: `save_plugin_state`.

### Letting a person pick the sound in the plugin UI (macOS, Windows)

For some plugins (such as Kontakt) the sound can only be loaded in their own UI, and neither parameters nor profiles can select it. In that case let a person pick:

- On the `muser view` page, the 🎛 next to each instrument track's name opens a "Sound" drawer from the right: "Built-in instruments" (muser's own synths, drum kits, keyboards..., searchable by name, category and description; click one to switch directly), "SFZ sampler" (the built-in sampler; click in to search
  the sounds in `$MUSER_SFZ_PATH`, click one to switch directly, written as a relative path), and below that the VST3 / CLAP instrument plugins scanned on this machine. Click a plugin to see the sounds that can be used directly
  (my sounds, captured ones, and presets that can be converted automatically such as Surge's .fxp; searchable, one click switches); for a new sound, give it a name and click "Load a new sound in <plugin>",
  pick and tweak it in the plugin's own browser, and click Done to save it into "My sounds"; "Adjust current sound" continues tweaking from this track's current sound and, when done, overwrites it under the original name.
  Which instruments Kontakt has (.nki names, sound libraries, tags) is not listed in the drawer; the agent looks them up with `muser sounds presets`. The command line works as well: `muser sounds presets / state / capture` (see "Choosing a sound" in SKILLS.md). A person picking sounds and tweaking parameters in the plugin window can play on the plugin's on-screen keyboard, or click "Audition this track" to loop the notes of this track (up to 8 bars).
  When the mouse is released in the window, a key is pressed, or the plugin reports a change, it is saved automatically after about 1.5 seconds and written back to the project (`@state` points to `<project name>.<track name>.muserstate` beside the project, and `@label` is the name), and view then re-renders.
  "Done" or closing the plugin window ends it; "Discard" restores the state from before it was opened.
- Command line: `muser plugin edit "<plugin>" [--params JSON] -o <file>`, which saves the state when the window is closed.
- `@label` is only a name for people and agents to read (the plugin's state is binary, and you cannot read out which sound was chosen), and is ignored when rendering.
  When the agent sees `"@label": "Piano Uno"` it knows what sound this track is; to change the sound, ask the person to pick again.
- On Windows / Linux there is no plugin window yet, and the panel lists only SFZ.

## 9. Multi-channel output and async loading (sampled drums, etc.)

Some plugins output each microphone separately (e.g. DrumGizmo's 15 channels: ambience, overheads, kick inside/outside, snare top/bottom...). By default only the first two are taken,
and that is often just the ambience mics, so the sound is distant and quiet. Use `@outputs` to specify how each channel is mixed into the stereo output:

```json
"instrument_params": {
  "@state": "kit.muserstate",
  "@warmup": 5,
  "@outputs": [
    { "channel": 1, "gain_db": -6, "pan": -1 },
    { "channel": 2, "gain_db": -6, "pan": 1 },
    { "channel": 8, "gain_db": 0, "pan": 0 },
    { "channel": 9, "gain_db": -8, "pan": 0, "invert": true }
  ]
}
```

- `channel` starts at 1 and is which channel of the plugin's main output (the "audio outputs" of `muser plugin info` gives the channel count); channels not listed do not enter the mix.
- `gain_db` defaults to 0; `pan` is between -1 (left) and 1 (right), default 0, with equal-power panning; `invert: true` inverts the phase (the snare bottom mic often needs it).
- `@warmup` (seconds, 0-60): after activation, run silently in real time and wait for the plugin to load samples on a background thread. A plugin like DrumGizmo loads the drum kit asynchronously,
  and offline rendering is much faster than real time, so without waiting the beginning is silent and the result differs each time. The cost is waiting this long before every render/start of playback.
- Which drum kit to load is stored in the plugin state: first get a state file with `muser plugin save-state`, then change the `drumkitfile` / `midimapfile` paths in it to the kit's location.

### Separate stems: each channel to its own bus (`bus`)

When an `@outputs` entry has `"bus": "<bus name>"`, that channel does **not go into this track** but goes straight into that bus (bypassing this track's effects and fader),
where you can attach effects, set volume, and make sends and sidechains on that bus alone; `muser mix-report` also reports the loudness bus by bus. Entries without `bus` are mixed into this track as usual.
The plugin plays only once, and all channels are taken out at the same time.

For the plugin's **auxiliary output buses** (Kontakt's Out 2, Out 3..., the zones of multi-output drum machines and organs) use `"aux": k` (the k-th after the main output, starting at 1,
listed in order under the "audio outputs" of `muser plugin info`) in place of `channel`: it takes the whole stereo pair, and `pan` is balance. muser opens the auxiliary outputs that are used.

```json
"buses": [
  { "name": "kick",  "effects": [{ "type": "transient_shaper", "attack_db": 4 }, { "type": "compressor", "threshold_db": -20, "ratio": 4 }] },
  { "name": "snare", "effects": [{ "type": "eq", "shape": "peak", "frequency": 200, "gain_db": 2 }], "sends": { "room": -12 } },
  { "name": "room",  "effects": [{ "type": "reverb", "mix": 1.0, "decay_seconds": 1.2 }] }
],
"tracks": [
  { "name": "kit", "instrument": "plugin:/Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/VST3/Kontakt 8.vst3#…",
    "instrument_params": { "@state": "kit.muserstate", "@outputs": [
      { "channel": 1, "pan": -1 }, { "channel": 2, "pan": 1 },
      { "aux": 1, "bus": "kick" },
      { "aux": 2, "bus": "snare" }
    ] } },
  { "name": "bass", "instrument": "bass.finger",
    "effects": [{ "type": "compressor", "threshold_db": -30, "ratio": 6, "sidechain": "kick" }] }
]
```

- Only the kick ducks the bass (`"sidechain": "kick"` names that bus), and the hi-hat no longer triggers it.
- **Which drum piece goes to which channel must be set in the plugin** (Kontakt: in the instrument's output settings / the kit mixer page, assign kick and snare to different Outs); the setting is stored with the plugin state:
  set it once in the plugin window (a person, or an agent using computer use), save it into the sound library with `muser sounds save`, and use it directly afterward.
- When this track is muted, all its direct outputs are muted together.
